summary: Read credentials from the environment instead of storing them in source code.
Bind a private service to the loopback interface instead of every network interface.
Use explicit byte decoding instead of converting a pointer with unsafe.
Handle the error from a filesystem operation instead of reporting success after a failed operation.
Audit the use of ssh.InsecureIgnoreHostKey function
Restrict HTTP fetches to approved destinations instead of accepting an arbitrary URL.
Register profiling handlers on a separate loopback server instead of exposing the default profiling routes on the public server.
Parse the requested signed integer width before converting the result to int32.
Bound the decompressed byte count when copying an archive entry to its output.
Serve a designated public directory instead of the filesystem root.
Set ReadHeaderTimeout on the HTTP server to bound the time allowed to read request headers.
Let the HTTP server frame the response instead of setting conflicting transfer-length headers.
Configure an http.Server with timeouts instead of calling a package-level serving function.
Reject values outside the target integer range before converting them.
Write bidirectional Unicode controls as explicit escapes instead of invisible source characters.
Exclude a password field from JSON serialization with a field tag.
Call the cancellation function returned by context.WithCancel.
Use Go's default redirect policy instead of copying authentication cookies to every redirect target.
Limit the total request body before reading a multipart form; the form's memory limit does not bound the upload size.
Limit cross-origin protection bypasses to the specific endpoint that requires one.
Delete files relative to an os.Root instead of reopening pathname strings that another process can replace during a directory walk.
Disable session tickets when custom certificate verification uses VerifyPeerCertificate and must run for every connection.
Set Secure, HttpOnly, and SameSite attributes on an authentication cookie.
Use SQL placeholders for a request value instead of formatting it into a query.
Pass a request value as a SQL argument instead of concatenating it into the query.
Let html/template escape page content instead of marking an untrusted string as trusted HTML.
Use a fixed executable instead of constructing its name from an environment variable.
Create a private directory with mode 0700 instead of granting access to every user.
Create a private file with mode 0600 instead of granting access to every user.
Use os.CreateTemp to create a temporary file with an unpredictable name.
Open a user-selected file relative to a confined os.Root instead of accepting an unrestricted path.
Extract archive entries relative to an os.Root to prevent paths from escaping the destination.
Write a private file with mode 0600 instead of granting access to every user.
When G307 configures a private permission mode, use os.OpenFile with mode 0600 instead of os.Create's default mode; the shared default does not restrict G307.
Use SHA-256 instead of MD5 for a cryptographic digest.
Require a supported TLS version when configuring a client connection.
Generate an RSA key with at least 2048 bits.
Use crypto/rand instead of math/rand for a security-sensitive random value.
Use AES instead of DES or RC4 for encryption.
Use SHA-256 instead of MD4 or RIPEMD-160 for a cryptographic digest.
Fill the entire encryption nonce with fresh cryptographic random bytes instead of leaving part of it unchanged.
Keep SSH public-key authentication state in the returned connection permissions and reject unauthorized keys with an error.
Import crypto/sha256 instead of the blocked crypto/md5 package.
Import crypto/aes instead of the blocked crypto/des package.
Import crypto/aes instead of the blocked crypto/rc4 package.
Serve dynamic content with a native HTTP handler instead of launching a CGI program.
Import crypto/sha256 instead of the blocked crypto/sha1 package.
Import crypto/sha256 instead of the blocked golang.org/x/crypto/md4 package.
Import crypto/sha256 instead of the blocked golang.org/x/crypto/ripemd160 package.
For Go versions before 1.22, avoid taking the address of the reused range value; Go 1.22 and later give each iteration its own value.
Check that the slice has enough elements before accessing a computed index.
Pass the untrusted user ID as a SQL argument instead of including it in the query text.
Select an approved executable instead of executing a command supplied by an HTTP request.
Fetch only an approved HTTP destination when the request supplies the URL.
Escape a request value before inserting it into an HTML response.
Quote a username before writing it to a text log to escape injected line breaks.
Validate both email envelope addresses before submitting the message to SMTP.
Use html/template to escape request values in an HTML page.
Bound the input before decoding an untrusted XML configuration.
Redirect to an approved local destination instead of an arbitrary URL supplied by the request.
